headline: Nearly 300 Humpback Whales Spotted in Rare Supergroup Off South Africa
meta_description: Nearly 300 humpback whales gathered off South Africa in what may be the largest supergroup ever recorded, marking a remarkable conservation success.
summary_short: Nearly 300 humpback whales were counted off South Africa in what may be the largest supergroup ever recorded, a stunning sign of population recovery.
body:
Nearly 300 humpback whales were counted off South Africa in what may be the largest supergroup ever recorded. The sighting represents a breathtaking moment for marine conservation.

This gathering reflects a much larger success story. Southern Hemisphere humpback populations have rebounded from fewer than 10,000 whales to more than 100,000 since commercial whaling ended. What was once a species hunted to the brink of extinction now congregates in numbers that researchers are still working to fully understand.

Supergroups—unusually large aggregations of whales—are themselves a subject of ongoing study. This sighting off South Africa may rank among the largest ever documented, offering scientists valuable data about whale behavior and the health of ocean ecosystems in the Southern Hemisphere.

May be the largest supergroup ever recorded
Southern Hemisphere populations grew from under 10,000 to over 100,000
